donts: Don't hide the QR code behind a tap or a popover.
Don't use mono for anything that is not an ID, code, or timestamp.
Don't add gradients, glass, or hard offset shadows to this system.
Don't swap the two directions — blue is always out, pink is always in.
Don't add a file manager to this screen — no categories, no storage gauges.
Don't use an eyebrow/kicker label above a heading.
dos: Do keep the QR code the largest, highest-contrast element on the screen.
Do pair every colour-coded state with a word ("Connected", "Listening…").
Do use 48px minimum touch targets for every action (52px for primary).
Do keep send progress honest: a real percentage from the transport, then a history entry.
Do keep the exchange illustration drawn from tokens — every fill and stroke is a var().
keyCharacteristics: Pale sky ground, white deck cards with soft shadows, heavily rounded (20px cards, pill buttons and tiles).
Deep blue is Send and primary; hot pink is the receive direction; green is listening and ready.
Nunito, a rounded geometric sans, self-hosted — extra-bold, tightly set headings.
Mono type only for IDs, codes, and timestamps — never as a costume.
Big touch targets, status always paired with a word, never colour alone.
narrative.overview: Two phones hand a file to each other across a pale sky, and the screen says so in the language of a share sheet: a big pill Send, a pink Receive, file rows with names and times, a small drawn exchange of two phones. Copied from Maveric's Dribbble file-sharing concept, mapped onto the transfer flow — the concept's file-manager content was left behind.

rules.body: Blue means out (send), pink means in (receive). Never swap them, and never use either as decoration.
rules.name: The Two-Direction Rule

rules.body: If it is not an ID, a code, or a timestamp, it is not set in mono.
rules.name: The Mono Is Data Rule

rules.body: Depth comes from soft offset shadows on deck cards and tiles. No hard offset shadows, no gradients, no glass.
rules.name: The Soft Shadow Rule
